facts.fact: UNESCO describes an eighteenth-century fortified town, influenced by European military planning within a North African context, with a history of international maritime trade.
facts.location: Visible source paragraph/table containing: fortified town
facts.excerpt: Maps Documents Gallery Video Indicators Assistance Medina of Essaouira (formerly Mogador) Essaouira is an exceptional example of a late-18th-century fortified town, built according to the principles of contemporary European military architecture in a North African context. Since its foundation, it has been a major international trading seaport, linking Morocco and its Saharan hinterland with Europe and the rest of the world.
